title: Truth of a Quantifier Prefix
statement: Let $P$ be a property of Boolean assignments $sigma : \mathbb{N} \to \{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$. The prefix is true at an assignment when its quantifiers can be evaluated in order starting at variable index $i$: an existential quantifier requires some Boolean value for the current variable, while a universal quantifier requires every Boolean value; after either choice, the assignment is updated at index $i$ and evaluation continues at index $i+1$. An empty prefix is true exactly when $P$ holds of the assignment.
hypotheses_covered: A list of existential and universal quantifiers
